content_html:
Check your agent for vulnerabilities before it goes into an air-gapped environment.

agent-blast-radius is an agent skill that reads an AI agent's codebase and answers two questions:

  1. Boundary: does anything in this agent need, or reach, the outside world? That covers hosted model APIs, telemetry that phones home, packages and models fetched at start, SaaS connectors and hard-coded external hosts.
  2. Blast radius: inside the enclave, if the agent is steered by a poisoned document, an insider or a compromised host, what can it do?

It writes a BLAST_RADIUS.md report with file:line evidence, the failure pattern each finding matches, OWASP agentic (ASI) ids, and the smallest fix for each path.

Why air-gapped agents need this

An air gap removes the network path out. It does not make an agent safe.

  • Agents leak by default. Hosted model clients send the whole context out on every call. Several frameworks export traces or telemetry to a vendor unless you opt out. In a sealed enclave these calls fail, and in a leaky one the data leaves.
  • Agents fetch code at start. npx -y some-mcp-server, pip install in a start script, and model downloads on first use all break the first time the agent boots inside the gap. Or, with a mirror, they run whatever the registry served that day.
  • The damage happens inside. Documented failures show agents deleting production databases and their backups with one call, leaking private data after reading a poisoned ticket, and serving as a path from one compromised laptop to other engineers' machines. None of these needed the internet. They needed an agent with more reach than its task.

What you get

From examples/sample-report.md, a run on the deliberately vulnerable examples/vulnerable-agent:

**Verdict:** CRITICAL · 4 critical, 7 high, 6 medium, 0 low
**Boundary:** LEAKY · 8 paths out

| What | Where | Crosses | When | Switch | Severity |
| Hosted model (support agent) | agent.py:51 | whole context: tickets, SQL results, emails | every call | none | HIGH |
| Issue-tracker MCP, unpinned | .mcp.json:3-5 (npx -y ...) | code in, newest release | every start | none | HIGH |

1. **CRITICAL**: ticket or web page → support agent → run_sql (DATABASE_URL, model-written SQL)
   → any write, delete or drop, no gate
   - Pattern: P02 · OWASP: ASI01, ASI02, ASI03
   - Fix: remove run_sql from the agent that reads tickets; typed read tools on a read-only role.

The report also includes a reach map (agent × tool × credential × gate), findings for each dimension, a detect-and-recover section, and a list of what static reading cannot prove.

Install

Claude Code (plugin)

Inside Claude Code 2.1.275 or later:

/plugin install agent-blast-radius --marketplace PrashnaLabs/agent-blast-radius

On older versions, add the marketplace first, then install:

/plugin marketplace add PrashnaLabs/agent-blast-radius
/plugin install agent-blast-radius@prashnalabs

The repository is private for now. Installing needs read access to it, and Claude Code clones it with your existing git credentials, so make sure git clone git@github.com:PrashnaLabs/agent-blast-radius.git works for you first (SSH key, or gh auth login). If background updates cannot reach it, export a GITHUB_TOKEN with read access.

Any Agent Skills host (manual)

Copy the skill folder into your agent's skills directory.

git clone git@github.com:PrashnaLabs/agent-blast-radius.git
cp -r agent-blast-radius/skills/agent-blast-radius ~/.claude/skills/          # all projects
# or: cp -r agent-blast-radius/skills/agent-blast-radius <your-repo>/.claude/skills/

The folder follows the Agent Skills layout (SKILL.md + references/ + scripts/), so other hosts that read Agent Skills can load it from their own skills directory. The skill itself needs no network access.

Use

In the repo you want audited, ask your agent:

is this agent ready for an air-gapped deployment?

or "audit my agent's blast radius", or "is this agent safe to ship?".

The scanner also runs on its own and prints JSON evidence:

python3 skills/agent-blast-radius/scripts/inventory.py path/to/repo

What it checks

Dimension Question
D8 Boundary What needs or reaches outside the enclave, and is there a switch to seal it?
D1 Untrusted input What attacker-controllable text reaches the context?
D2 Reach What systems, data and credentials can the agent touch?
D3 Privilege fit Is each credential scoped to the task?
D4 Irreversibility Which reachable actions cannot be undone?
D5 Egress Where can data go?
D6 Gates What stands between the model's decision and the action, enforced in code?
D7 Identity & audit Can you prove who did what, and stop it?

The report has two verdict lines:

  • Boundary: SEALED (nothing crosses), BRITTLE (nothing leaks, but something is fetched at start), or LEAKY (context leaves by default).
  • Blast radius: CRITICAL (a toxic path or lethal trifecta), EXPOSED (high-severity reach), or CONTAINED (every irreversible action is gated and audited).

The full rules are in references/rubric.md.

Frameworks: LangChain, LangGraph, deepagents, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents SDK, Claude Agent SDK, Vercel AI SDK, raw tool-calling loops, and MCP client configs, in Python and TypeScript, plus Dockerfiles and start scripts.

How it works

Two halves keep the judgment honest:

  1. scripts/inventory.py: a deterministic, read-only scanner that uses only the Python standard library and needs no network. It never imports or runs your code and never prints secret values; credentials appear by name and location only. It lists every external host found in code, and the same repo always gives the same JSON.
  2. SKILL.md: the agent reads each tool and boundary crossing the scanner points at, decides what really crosses or is reachable, traces the toxic paths, and scores them against a fixed rubric. Whether a send tool's "only call this after the user confirms" is enforced by the server or only written in a docstring needs reading the code. A linter cannot decide it.

Findings cite patterns from references/patterns.md: documented agent failures and risky library defaults, described without naming the organisations involved.

Safety

  • Read-only. The only file it writes is BLAST_RADIUS.md, and it asks before overwriting one.
  • It never runs, installs or connects to anything in the target repo.
  • Secret values are never printed.
  • The scanner runs fully offline.

Limits

  • Static only. It cannot see network policy, IAM policies, token scopes, or the tools a remote MCP server serves at runtime. These go under "Unverifiable statically", with where to check.
  • The scanner matches line by line, so it can miss calls split across lines. The reading step covers most of these.
  • The scanner takes about 1 s of CPU per MB of source. In a large monorepo, point it at the agent's directory.

Development

uvx pytest -q tests

tests/test_inventory.py checks the scanner against the fixture: every expected hit and no extra hits, the build-time versus runtime install rule, the external host summary, secret redaction, vendor-directory skipping and the per-rule cap. examples/vulnerable-agent/expected.md is the golden set for the skill itself.

License

Apache-2.0

   - Pattern: P02 · OWASP: ASI01, ASI02, ASI03
   - Fix: remove run_sql from the agent that reads tickets; typed read tools on a read-only role.

The report also includes a reach map (agent × tool × credential × gate), findings for each dimension, a detect-and-recover section, and a list of what static reading cannot prove.

安装

Claude Code (plugin)

Inside Claude Code 2.1.275 or later:

/plugin install agent-blast-radius --marketplace PrashnaLabs/agent-blast-radius

On older versions, add the marketplace first, then install:

/plugin marketplace add PrashnaLabs/agent-blast-radius
/plugin install agent-blast-radius@prashnalabs

The repository is private for now. Installing needs read access to it, and Claude Code clones it with your existing git credentials, so make sure git clone git@github.com:PrashnaLabs/agent-blast-radius.git works for you first (SSH key, or gh auth login). If background updates cannot reach it, export a GITHUB_TOKEN with read access.

Any Agent Skills host (manual)

Copy the skill folder into your agent's skills directory.

git clone git@github.com:PrashnaLabs/agent-blast-radius.git
cp -r agent-blast-radius/skills/agent-blast-radius ~/.claude/skills/          # all projects
# or: cp -r agent-blast-radius/skills/agent-blast-radius <your-repo>/.claude/skills/

The folder follows the Agent Skills layout (SKILL.md + references/ + scripts/), so other hosts that read Agent Skills can load it from their own skills directory. The skill itself needs no network access.

Use

In the repo you want audited, ask your agent:

is this agent ready for an air-gapped deployment?

or "audit my agent's blast radius", or "is this agent safe to ship?".

The scanner also runs on its own and prints JSON evidence:

python3 skills/agent-blast-radius/scripts/inventory.py path/to/repo

它检查什么

方面 问题
D8 边界 What needs or reaches outside the enclave, and is there a switch to seal it?
D1 Untrusted input What attacker-controllable text reaches the context?
D2 Reach What systems, data and credentials can the agent touch?
D3 Privilege fit Is each credential scoped to the task?
D4 Irreversibility Which reachable actions cannot be undone?
D5 出口 Where can data go?
D6 Gates What stands between the model's decision and the action, enforced in code?
D7 Identity & audit Can you prove who did what, and stop it?

The report has two verdict lines:

  • Boundary: SEALED (nothing crosses), BRITTLE (nothing leaks, but something is fetched at start), or LEAKY (context leaves by default).
  • Blast radius: CRITICAL (a toxic path or lethal trifecta), EXPOSED (high-severity reach), or CONTAINED (every irreversible action is gated and audited).

The full rules are in references/rubric.md.

Frameworks: LangChain, LangGraph, deepagents, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents SDK, Claude Agent SDK, Vercel AI SDK, raw tool-calling loops, and MCP client configs, in Python and TypeScript, plus Dockerfiles and start scripts.

它是如何运作的

Two halves keep the judgment honest:

  1. scripts/inventory.py: a deterministic, read-only scanner that uses only the Python standard library and needs no network. It never imports or runs your code and never prints secret values; credentials appear by name and location only. It lists every external host found in code, and the same repo always gives the same JSON.
  2. SKILL.md: the agent reads each tool and boundary crossing the scanner points at, decides what really crosses or is reachable, traces the toxic paths, and scores them against a fixed rubric. Whether a send tool's "only call this after the user confirms" is enforced by the server or only written in a docstring needs reading the code. A linter cannot decide it.

Findings cite patterns from references/patterns.md: documented agent failures and risky library defaults, described without naming the organisations involved.

安全

  • 只读。 The only file it writes is BLAST_RADIUS.md, and it asks before overwriting one.
  • It never runs, installs or connects to anything in the target repo.
  • Secret values are never printed.
  • The scanner runs fully offline.

限制

  • Static only. It cannot see network policy, IAM policies, token scopes, or the tools a remote MCP server serves at runtime. These go under "Unverifiable statically", with where to check.
  • The scanner matches line by line, so it can miss calls split across lines. The reading step covers most of these.
  • The scanner takes about 1 s of CPU per MB of source. In a large monorepo, point it at the agent's directory.

发展

uvx pytest -q tests

tests/test_inventory.py checks the scanner against the fixture: every expected hit and no extra hits, the build-time versus runtime install rule, the external host summary, secret redaction, vendor-directory skipping and the per-rule cap. examples/vulnerable-agent/expected.md is the golden set for the skill itself.
